title: Operator microtask mesh and playbook scaffolding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight microtask mesh that converts traditional runbooks into composable, idempotent tasks and a scaffolder that auto-generates playbook fragments from incident transcripts. Goal: reduce mean time to remediate by letting first-line engineers execute small, auditable tasks rather than long procedural docs. Integrate scaffolder with RBAC/audit logs and add a dry-run simulator for safe validation.
acceptance_criteria: Scaffolder can ingest a short incident transcript (<= 5 messages) and emit at least 3 candidate microtasks with suggested inputs and preconditions.
A microtask runtime endpoint accepts tasks and returns deterministic success/failure with structured logs and tokenized telemetry for tracing in Console.
All executed microtasks create audit entries that include invoked_by, task_id, input_hash, and a per-run idempotency token.
Dry-run simulator can execute tasks in a non-mutating mode and produce a report with side-effect estimations and a confidence score.
Playbook scaffolder UI flow exists as a Console modal prototype and links back to Confluence docs and a GitHub starter PR template.
Security review completed and KMS integration plan documented for secrets used by task runners.
tasks: Design microtask schema (idempotency token, inputs, preconditions, outputs, compensating action)
Implement task registration API and lightweight runtime for synchronous microtasks
Build scaffolder model/heuristic: transcript -> candidate tasks + suggested inputs
Console modal prototype for 'Scaffold playbook from chat' and API contract
Add audit logging hooks (CloudAudit-compatible) and KMS secret access patterns
Implement dry-run simulator with sandboxed adapters for DB/infra operations
End-to-end test harness: synthetic incident -> scaffold -> dry-run -> live-runbackfill
Documentation: Confluence spec + runbook templates + GitHub PR template
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly broad auto-generated tasks could perform dangerous actions. Mitigation: default to read-only suggestions in scaffolder and require explicit privileged approval for write tasks.
Risk: Latency overhead if tasks are chained synchronously. Mitigation: support async task chaining and backpressure-aware scheduling in runtime.
Risk: Audit volume growth. Mitigation: add sample-rate controls and summarized audit rollups in Console.
Risk: Secrets leak from scaffolder suggestions. Mitigation: mask secrets in UI and require KMS-unseal at runtime only after RBAC checks.
notes: Inspiration: autogen snippets used by support teams at other infra companies; aim for human-in-the-loop generation rather than full automation.
Prototype experiments (see PR #482 in github.com/redwood-inference/opsflow) show 40% faster first-run completion when engineers use two microtasks vs a single manual runbook.
We should reuse the existing runbook-telemetry schema from ENG-214501 to keep Console dashboards consistent.
Prefer explicit task contracts vs freeform scripts to enable safe dry-run and idempotency guarantees.
deliverables: API spec (OpenAPI) for microtask registration and execution
Scaffolder service (binary + lightweight model heuristics) with a small dataset of annotated incident->task examples
Console modal prototype and user flow doc
Dry-run simulator service and e2e test suite
Confluence spec and migration guide for converting 10 canonical runbooks into microtask sets
